sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Bremerton?
sections.html:
Selling a house in Bremerton starts with the Navy. The city of 45,482 residents (Census Bureau estimate, July 1, 2025) is the largest on the Kitsap Peninsula and is home to Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and the Bremerton Annex of Naval Base Kitsap. Owners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or accept a cash offer.

William Bremer, a German immigrant and real estate agent, founded the town in 1891, the same year the Navy bought about 190 acres of his waterfront land on Sinclair Inlet for $50 an acre. Bremerton incorporated on October 15, 1901. Since 1985 it has been a first-class city with a strong mayor and a seven-member council. Downtown has been rebuilt in stages since a boardwalk and marina opened in 1992, and City Hall has been housed in the Norm Dicks Government Center since 2004.

sections.h2: How do the shipyard, ferries and bridges shape buyer demand in Bremerton?
sections.html:
Commute routes decide which Bremerton blocks sell fastest. The Port Washington Narrows cuts the city in two, and two bridges join the halves: the Warren Avenue Bridge on State Route 303, opened in 1958, and the Manette Bridge, rebuilt in 2011. State Route 3 runs as a freeway through the west side and a tunnel carries ferry traffic from the terminal to State Route 304.

Washington State Ferries takes about an hour from Bremerton to Seattle, and in 2024 that route carried 990,435 passengers. Kitsap Transit's passenger-only fast ferry covers the crossing in 28 minutes. Buyers who work at the shipyard or across the water may ask how far a house sits from the terminal or the gates.

  • Downtown and the waterfront have new apartments, restored older buildings and the Admiral Theatre.
  • Manette sits on its own peninsula, was annexed in 1918 and reaches downtown over the Manette Bridge.
  • Charleston grew as a sailors' town, joined the city in 1927 and centers on Callow Avenue.
  • Union Hill is mostly residential and lies between downtown and Charleston.
  • Evergreen has water views and a park with a beach and boat ramp.
  • Haddon surrounds Bremerton High School and the Olympic College campus.

Three school districts reach into the city: Bremerton, Central Kitsap and South Kitsap. Confirm the district for your address before you put it in a listing.

sections.h2: How does Bremerton weather affect an older house?
sections.html: Bremerton has warm, dry summers and wet, mild winters. Rainfall averages 56.93 inches a year, while snow averages about 3 inches. The wettest year on record, 1999, brought 75.81 inches. With that much water, roofs, gutters, siding, crawl spaces and drainage deserve attention before a showing or an inspection. The city sits in USDA climate zone 8.

sections.h2: What does the Bremerton landlord license mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Anyone who rents or leases real property inside Bremerton limits needs a City of Bremerton Landlord Business License under BMC 3.48.025. It is a city license, separate from any Washington state business license, and it costs $75 a year. Licenses run January 1 through December 31 and renewals are due by January 31.

  • Renting rooms inside your own home counts as rental activity.
  • A relative living in the house counts as a rental even without rent, unless the owner also lives there more than half the year.
  • Landlords join the Landlord Notification Program (BMC 5.06) by giving the Police Department a list of rentals and a contact method.
  • Landlords certify that units meet RCW 59.18.060, and the city does not run physical inspections.
  • Stays under 30 days, such as vacation rentals, fall under state business licensing instead.

The city warns that an unlicensed property may limit the owner's ability to pursue an eviction. If you inherited a Bremerton rental, bring the license in line before you list it, and call the Tax and License Division at 360-473-5311 with questions.

sections.h2: What does a Bremerton seller owe at closing?
sections.html:
The seller pays real estate excise tax, and the Kitsap County Treasurer collects it. Kitsap lists the local portion at 0.50 percent, and the state portion is graduated. On a sale at the Census median value of $439,400, the state portion is 1.1 percent of the full price, or $4,833.40, because the price sits under the $525,000 first band. The local 0.50 percent adds $2,197, for about $7,030 in total, plus a $5 state technology fee. Ask the treasurer to confirm the total for your parcel.

  • The tax is due within 30 days of the date on the conveying document and must be paid before the deed can be recorded.
  • The Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit must be signed by seller and buyer, or by an agent for each.
  • The treasurer takes cash or check payable to the Kitsap County Treasurer, and cards carry fees.
  • Late payment adds interest and penalties under RCW 82.45.100, which reach 20 percent of the tax after three months.

For sales starting January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue moves the state break points to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000.

sections.h2: How does Kitsap County bill property tax to Bremerton owners?
sections.html:
Kitsap County bills in two halves. The first is due April 30 and the balance October 31, payments count if postmarked by those dates, and a bill of $50 or less is due in full in April. For residential property with four or fewer units, delinquent tax carries interest of 0.75 percent a month, which matches the nine percent a year in RCW 84.56.020. There is no general good cause waiver. Failing to receive a statement does not erase interest.

Escrow deserves a look. Kitsap warns that tax money collected at a refinance is sometimes not forwarded to the treasurer until April or October, so confirm the account shows as paid before you list. The Assessor's Office, reachable at (360) 337-5777, handles the senior and disabled exemption and deferral, the limited-income deferral, the residential improvement exemption and the destroyed property exemption. State law also bars interest and penalties on the home of an active duty service member stationed outside the United States during a period of armed conflict.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a Bremerton house quickly?
sections.html:
Orders to a new duty station, an inherited rental or a house that needs work all push owners toward a faster sale. The routes are familiar.

  • List with an agent and time showings around the weekend crowds that fill downtown for events such as the Armed Forces Day parade in May and the Blackberry Festival over Labor Day.
  • Sell the house yourself, handling the disclosure statement and the excise tax affidavit on your own.
  • Request a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is, which can avoid repairs and open houses.

Whichever route you choose, hand the buyer the seller disclosure statement within five business days after the contract is signed unless it is waived or exempt, since RCW 64.06.020 gives the buyer three business days to rescind once it arrives.

faqs.q: How much does a Bremerton seller pay in excise tax?
faqs.a: It depends on the price. The state portion starts at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, and Kitsap County lists the local portion at 0.50 percent. At $439,400 that comes to about $7,030, plus a $5 state technology fee.

faqs.q: Does Bremerton require a license to rent out a house?
faqs.a: Yes. Anyone renting real property inside city limits needs a Bremerton Landlord Business License, which costs $75 a year and renews by January 31. The city does not inspect the unit and relies on the landlord's certification.

faqs.q: When are Kitsap County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second half. Payments must be postmarked by those dates, and a bill of $50 or less is due in full on April 30.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bremerton house I inherited with tenants inside?
faqs.a: Yes, but confirm the Landlord Business License is current first, because an unlicensed property can limit the owner's eviction options. Review the lease and ask the Tax and License Division at 360-473-5311 about the license record.

faqs.q: How can I confirm a house is inside Bremerton city limits?
faqs.a: Enter the address in the Kitsap County Parcel Search, the tool the city points owners to. City limits decide whether the landlord license and other city rules apply.
